excluded_source_media.reason: Joint project logo, not an analytical figure.

publication_note: Original report snapshots, including historical visuals with explicitly documented interpretation and validation limits. No original file, raw game rows or custom-visual code distributed.

figures.title: Shooting percentages by opponent
figures.caption: Saved opponent view of average game-level FG%, FT% and 3P%; it is a displayed snapshot, not every opponent or an attempt-weighted shooting rate.

figures.title: Calendar-year production trend
figures.caption: Calendar-year averages of points, rebounds and assists; NBA-season workbook averages must be interpreted separately.

figures.title: Average scoring in wins and losses
figures.caption: The displayed percentages normalize two scoring averages; they are not shares of games or total points and establish no causal effect.

figures.title: Original forecast display — unvalidated
figures.caption: Historical saved forecast shown for completeness; assumptions, validation and accuracy are unverified, so it is not offered as a future-performance prediction.

figures.title: Selected-peer scoring and plus-minus
figures.caption: Average points and plus/minus for six selected guards; this is not a league-wide ranking or causal-impact estimate.

figures.title: Selected-peer radar comparison
figures.caption: Original Microsoft custom-visual snapshot of average assists, points and rebounds; the measures share a raw scale and are not a normalized overall-skill score.

figures.title: Turnovers and personal fouls
figures.caption: Per-game averages for six selected guards in the saved report context; usage and role differ, so this is not a role-adjusted error-rate ranking.

figures.title: Selected-peer shooting percentages
figures.caption: Averages of game-level FG%, FT% and 3P%; these can differ from rates computed from total makes and attempts.

figures.title: Selected-peer scoring totals
figures.caption: Recorded points, made free throws and made three-pointers; totals depend on games played and availability and do not by themselves prove consistency.
